column1: # Which area (tools\check-areas.tsv) a changed file belongs to, for tools\select-checks.ps1 (read by tools\CheckSelector.cs).
# One rule per line: a regular expression on the file's path in the repository (forward slashes, case-sensitive), then
# the area or areas it selects (comma-separated). A file takes every rule it matches, so a file can select several areas.
# A file that matches no rule selects "full": the selector never guesses a file it cannot place.
# Files that draw nothing and are proven by other checks: the .NET suite (tests), running the live script (live checks).
# The check scripts themselves: a change to how checks run is proven by the full set.
# full because: these scripts start, drive and guard every render and test run, so a change to one can alter any case and no narrower set shows it.
# full because: it places the window every render run opens; a fault in it shows in any case.
# Build and tool settings shared by everything.
# full because: project, package and solution settings decide how every project builds and which versions it runs against; any picture can change.
# full because: vendored libraries and data (parsers, keyword lists, native physics) are loaded by the whole viewer; no one area owns them.
# full because: engine project settings (rendering, windows, export) apply to every picture on both backends.
# full because: a shader is compiled for and used by every case that draws with it, across areas.
# The engine side: what every picture goes through.
# full because: the render harness and the engine start-up, window and diagnostics code run in every render case.
# full because: the world presenter, texture hub, warm-up and engine-resource bookkeeping draw or free everything every case shows.
# full because: the camera, the capture replay and the platform paths and settings are read by every render run (the replay feeds the world model as the session does).
# World files whose users the code shows: only the areas of those users, found by who names each file's types in host and core
# (the engine layer that draws it, its own render cases). The sky and the water are drawn by EnvironmentLayer.
# WaterPlan: the environment layer's water and the neighbour stack's water (terrain). SkyProbe and ToneMap: the sky layer and the avatar skin-light cases.
# Glow and the projector picture: the prim layer and the glow pass (objects). Glow and AutoMask are also read by the avatar face shader.
# GlowOccluders: the glow pass and the terrain view. TreeNoise: the tree mesher (trees are in the terrain and object cases).
# LookSummary: read only by the neighbour code. BlendOrder: blended faces, the face shader, the environment layer and the face rules.

# full because: any other World file (WorldState, the object table, materials, lights, motion, appearance, trees, terrain data) is the shared model the protocol fills and every layer reads, or is used by a hub or the session as well; the code shows no narrower set. A new World file lands here until it is placed above.
# Main.cs alone: one render case from each area on Vulkan; the next full gate runs the full set.
# full because: the presentation policy, frame budget, camera, backend choice and device code in the shell decide how every picture is drawn and paced.
# The interface: the theme and the frame are shared by every window, so they run every interface case.
# Login, the session and the grid's services: the login pictures and the stock smoke.
# The edit controller sends the object and build updates.
# The sky, the water and the light.
# The one kept read of the window's picture: the proportions case (avatars) and the chat bar part of the exported-build smoke (login).
# Appearance and outfits send and read wearables, bakes and outfit folders.
# Objects: prims, meshes, textures, materials, glow.
# Files that were not placed before; each placed by what its code does.

# Draw nothing and are proven by the unit tests, S-1 or the stock smoke: the core's identity string, the data the unit tests read, S-1's physics-library check, the test-only crash switch, an engine ignore file, the keyword generator.
# Measuring code the render harness and the start-up log use: one sample case from each area shows if it broke.
# full because: CompileWatch counts the pipelines compiled in every render run and the pre-warm-up and busy-scene code report through it.
# full because: Main.tscn is the main scene every run of the viewer opens, so any picture can change.
# full because: the host solution file lists the host projects and is the same kind of file as Viewer.sln above.
# The S-1 smoke scene belongs with S1Smoke.cs (login).
# Interface: the Gestures window reads the Gestures inventory folder; the link strip, the window mode and the mouse-look setting are interface code.
# Interface: the Snapshot window and taking its pictures.
# The soak run (test only) cycles the object scenes.
# The quit watchdog draws nothing, but it runs on the quit path: a stuck quit is ended by it. Only a real start followed by a real quit
# exercises that, and the stock smoke does both, so it selects the smoke and no render case (a "none" here skipped the one check that reaches it).
